questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution specifically mentions the power of the State to regulate the burden of taxation?
questions.explanation: Article 282 specifically mentions the power of the State to regulate the burden of taxation.

questions.question: What is the name of the highest court in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Calcutta High Court is the highest court in West Bengal.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following is a fundamental duty of every citizen?
options: To uphold the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions
questions.explanation: To uphold the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions is a fundamental duty of every citizen.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Panchayati Raj system in West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Panchayati Raj system in West Bengal has a three-tier Panchayat structure.

questions.question: What is the term for the separation of powers among the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of the government in India?
questions.explanation: The separation of powers is the term for the separation of powers among the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of the government in India.

questions.question: Which one of the following rivers originates from the Himalayas and flows through West Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Teesta River originates from the Himalayas in Tibet.

questions.explanation: The Chhotanagpur Plateau is a part of the eastern Deccan Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest peak in the Darjeeling Himalayan hill region?
questions.explanation: Sandakphu is the highest peak in the Darjeeling Himalayan hill region.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through the Sundarbans delta?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans delta is formed by the combined flow of the Ganges, Hooghly, and Brahmaputra rivers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a prominent island in the Sundarbans delta?
questions.explanation: Gangasagar Island is a prominent island in the Sundarbans delta.

questions.question: Under the Swasthya Sathi Scheme, what is the primary goal?
options: To provide cashless treatment to all citizens
To provide free treatment to patients in government hospitals
To cover 10 crore families under health insurance
To reduce out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare
questions.explanation: The Swasthya Sathi Scheme aims to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure on healthcare.

questions.question: The Kanyashree Prakalpa is an initiative launched by the West Bengal government to?
options: Provide financial assistance to girls for education
Support girls in rural areas for higher education
Promote girls' education and prevent child marriage
questions.explanation: This initiative promotes girls' education and prevents child marriage.

questions.question: The Duare Duare Ration Scheme was launched by the state government to provide?
options: Ration to the poor and underprivileged communities
Ration to the people of North Bengal
Ration to the people of South Bengal
Ration to the people of Kolkata
questions.explanation: The Duare Duare Ration Scheme aims to provide ration to the poor and underprivileged communities.

questions.question: The Sakha (One Stop Centre) Scheme was launched by the West Bengal government to?
options: Provide shelter to women in distress
Provide legal aid to women in distress
Provide counseling and support to women in distress
Provide emergency assistance to women in distress
questions.explanation: The Sakha (One Stop Centre) Scheme provides counseling and support to women in distress.

questions.question: The Banglar Krishi Bikash (BKB) Scheme was launched by the state government to?
options: Promote organic farming in West Bengal
Increase crop production and productivity in West Bengal
Provide financial assistance to farmers in West Bengal
Promote irrigation facilities in West Bengal
questions.explanation: The Banglar Krishi Bikash (BKB) Scheme aims to increase crop production and productivity in West Bengal.

questions.question: A pump can fill 1/4th of a tank in 10 minutes. It can fill 3/4th of the tank in?
questions.explanation: The remaining 1/4th of the tank will take 10 minutes to fill.

questions.question: A man can do a piece of work in 10 days, if he works 4 hours a day. How many hours a day will he work to finish the work in 5 days?
questions.explanation: He needs to work more hours a day to complete the work in 5 days.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours respectively. If they work together, they can fill the tank in?
questions.explanation: When pipes A and B work together, their combined rate of work increases.

questions.question: A tap can fill 1/2 of a cistern in 1 hour and another tap can fill 1/4 of the cistern in 1 hour. If both taps work together, they can fill the cistern in?
questions.explanation: They can fill the cistern together in less than 1 hour.

questions.question: A well can be filled by a pipe in 20 days. If 2/5th of the pipe's capacity is used to fill the well, in how many days will the well be filled?
questions.explanation: The rate of filling the well is directly proportional to the capacity of the pipe.

questions.question: A train covers a distance of 240 km in 8 hours. How much distance will it cover in 24 hours?
questions.explanation: Distance covered is directly proportional to the time taken.

questions.question: A person travels from Kolkata to Siliguri at an average speed of 60 km/h. How many hours will he take to cover a distance of 360 km?
questions.explanation: Time taken is inversely proportional to the speed.

questions.question: Two cyclists start from the same point and travel in opposite directions. One travels at 15 km/h and the other at 10 km/h. What is their relative speed?
questions.explanation: Relative speed is the sum of individual speeds.

questions.question: A bus travels from Durgapur to Asansol at an average speed of 50 km/h and returns back at an average speed of 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed for the entire journey is the harmonic mean of the individual speeds.

questions.question: A train is traveling from Sealdah to Bardhaman at an average speed of 80 km/h. If it is traveling for 3 hours, how much distance will it cover in the last 45 minutes?
questions.explanation: Distance covered is directly proportional to the time taken.

questions.question: A man walks 8 km towards the north and then walks 4 km towards the east. He then walks 4 km due south. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: The man is 5 km away from his starting point.

questions.question: A tourist is at Howrah Bridge in Kolkata. He sees a park to his east, a river to his south, and a statue in the city to his west. In which direction is the city railway station located?
questions.explanation: The city railway station is located in the North direction.

questions.question: A man walks 12 km due east and then 6 km due west. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: He is still 12 km away from his starting point.

questions.question: A tourist is at the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway station. He sees a hill to his east and the city of Darjeeling to his north. In which direction is the tea garden located?
questions.explanation: The tea garden is located in the East direction.

questions.question: A man walks 5 km towards the north, then 5 km towards the east, 2 km due south, and finally 1 km west. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: He is still 5 km away from his starting point due to the Pythagorean theorem.
